title: Maximal atlases without Zorn's lemma
promptMarkdown:
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff, second countable space and $\mathcal{A}$ an atlas on $X$. Define
$$\mathcal{A}_{\max}=\{(V,\psi)\text{ a chart on }X:\ (V,\psi)\text{ is compatible with every chart of }\mathcal{A}\}.$$

1. Prove that any two charts in $\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ are compatible with each other, so $\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ is an atlas. (Smoothness of a map between open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a local property; use the charts of $\mathcal{A}$ to test it.)
2. Prove that $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ and that $\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ is maximal.
3. Prove that $\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ is the only maximal atlas containing $\mathcal{A}$.
4. Deduce that two atlases are equivalent (their union is an atlas) if and only if they determine the same maximal atlas.

The notes' Exercise 1 suggests Zorn's lemma for the existence of a maximal atlas. Say in one sentence why no choice principle is needed.
hintLadder: Take $(V,\psi),(W,\chi)\in\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ and a point $x\in V\cap W$. Some chart $(U,\varphi)$ of $\mathcal{A}$ contains $x$. Write $\chi\circ\psi^{-1}$ near $\psi(x)$ as a composition of two transition maps that you know are smooth.
Be explicit about the open set on which the composition is defined: $\psi(U\cap V\cap W)$.
For uniqueness, show that any maximal atlas $\mathcal{M}\supseteq\mathcal{A}$ satisfies $\mathcal{M}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{\max}$, and then that $\mathcal{M}\cup\mathcal{A}_{\max}$ is an atlas.

criteria.criterion: Compatibility of two charts of A_max is proved by factoring the transition map through a chart of A on an explicitly named open set, for an arbitrary point of the overlap.

levels.description: Composition and domains explicit; both directions covered.

Equivalence of atlases characterised correctly and the remark on Zorn made accurately (the maximal atlas is defined explicitly, so no choice is needed).
